exposure: Cervical strain assessed with quasi-static elastography (in sagittal plane, at internal cervical os, and external cervical os)
outcome: Spontaneous preterm delivery at <=34 weeks of gestation
Spontaneous preterm delivery at <37 weeks of gestation
cohort: The study included 545 pregnant women with singleton pregnancies.
finding: Increased strain in the internal cervical os, particularly in the 3rd and 4th quartiles, is associated with a significantly higher risk of spontaneous preterm delivery at <=34 weeks and <37 weeks of gestation.
cross-section timing: Cervical strain was evaluated between 11 weeks and 28 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: Exposure measurement was performed from 11 weeks to 28 weeks of gestation, and outcomes were defined at <=34 weeks and <37 weeks of gestation.
